facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Vitirallus.
The only known species in this genus is Vitirallus watlingi.
Trevor H. Worthy first described the species in 2004.
facts.quote: It was first described by Trevor H. Worthy in 2004.

facts.statement: Fossil remains were discovered in September 1998 on the island of Viti Levu.
facts.quote: Remains of this species were discovered in September 1998 at Viti Levu

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Late Pleistocene and Early Holocene.
Its time range is recorded from 0.129 million years ago to the present Holocene.
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: Vitirallus watlingi is the type species for the genus.
It was a prehistoric flightless bird known as the Fiji rail or Viti Levu rail.
facts.quote: Vitirallus watlingi, the Fiji rail or Viti Levu rail, was a prehistoric flightless bird from Fiji

facts.statement: It possessed a very elongated and slender bill.
facts.quote: but with a very elongated and slender bill

facts.statement: The genus name refers to Viti Levu, the island where it originated in Fiji.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to Viti Levu, the island of origin in Fiji

facts.statement: The part of the name 'rallus' is Latin for rail.
The species name 'watlingi' honors the ornithologist Dr. Dick Watling.
facts.quote: The species name watlingi is after the ornithologist Dr. Dick Watling.

rejected.statement: It is thought to have been about the same size as the bar-winged rail.
rejected.quote: Vitirallus watlingi is thought to have been about the same size as the bar-winged rail (Nesoclopeus poecilopterus)
